title: NEB Class 11 Physics — Circular Motion — 2024
subject: physics
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Define centripetal acceleration. Derive an expression for it.
questions.solution:
**Centripetal acceleration** is the acceleration of a body in circular motion, directed toward the centre of the circle.

Derivation: a particle moves on radius r with uniform speed v. In time Δt it sweeps angle Δθ. The velocity vector turns through the same angle, so the change Δv ≈ v·Δθ (small angles).

a = Δv/Δt = v(Δθ/Δt) = vω = v(v/r) = **v²/r** (equivalently a = ω²r).
questions.knowledgeNote: Centripetal force F = mv²/r is not a new force — it is the name for whatever net force (tension, friction, gravity) provides the centre-seeking acceleration.

questions.question: A car takes a turn of radius 50 m at a speed of 10 m/s. What is its angular velocity and centripetal acceleration?
questions.solution:
Angular velocity ω = v/r = 10/50 = **0.2 rad/s**.

Centripetal acceleration ac = v²/r = 100/50 = **2 m/s²** toward the centre of the turn.
questions.knowledgeNote: ω = v/r and T = 2π/ω link the linear and angular descriptions — convert rpm to rad/s before using them.

questions.question: Derive the expression for the angle of banking of a curved road, and find the banking angle for a 100 m radius curve taken at 20 m/s. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.solution:
On a banked curve (angle θ), the normal reaction N has components N sin θ (horizontal, provides centripetal force) and N cos θ (vertical, balances weight).

N sin θ = mv²/r and N cos θ = mg → dividing gives tan θ = **v²/(rg)**.

tan θ = 400/(100 × 10) = 0.4 → θ = **21.8°**.
questions.knowledgeNote: Banking lets the road itself supply the centripetal force, so vehicles need less friction — that is why expressway curves are tilted.

questions.question: A stone is whirled in a vertical circle of radius 1 m. What is the minimum velocity it must have at the top of the circle to complete the loop? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.solution:
At the top, both weight and tension point downward: mv²/r = mg + T. The loop is just completed when the string goes slack, T = 0.

v² = gr → v = √(9.8 × 1) ≈ **3.13 m/s**.
questions.knowledgeNote: Minimum top velocity √(gr); the matching bottom velocity is √(5gr) — the 1:√5 ratio is a standard NEB result.

questions.question: A conical pendulum has a string 1 m long making 30° with the vertical. Calculate its period of revolution. (g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.knowledgeNote: The period depends on the vertical height h = l cos θ, not on the mass of the bob.

questions.question: A wheel of diameter 0.8 m rotates at 300 revolutions per minute. Find its angular velocity and the linear speed of a point on its rim.
questions.solution:
Frequency f = 300/60 = 5 rev/s.

ω = 2πf = 10π ≈ **31.4 rad/s**.

Rim speed v = ωr = 31.4 × 0.4 ≈ **12.6 m/s**.
questions.knowledgeNote: Always convert rpm → rev/s → rad/s first; most NEB errors here come from using rpm directly in v = ωr.
